title: Abort, retry, and let git pick a side for you
summary: Get out of a merge cleanly, then learn the strategy options that resolve whole classes of conflict automatically — and exactly when using them is a mistake.
mental_model: `-X ours` is a tie-breaker inside a normal merge: take our side of conflicting hunks, keep everything else merged. `-s ours` is a completely different beast: throw away their changes entirely and keep our tree. One letter, opposite risk.
danger: `-s ours` discards the other branch's work while recording a merge that claims to include it. Later merges will believe those commits are already in. Use it only when you genuinely mean 'mark this as merged without taking anything'.

commit.message: Raise retries and timeout after the incident

steps.title: Start a merge and hit the conflict
steps.why: Both branches changed `retries`. The timeout change on main and the new file on the branch merge cleanly — only the one contested line stops the process.
steps.expect: CONFLICT on config.yaml; tuning.md merges in silently.

steps.title: Get out of it entirely
steps.why: `--abort` restores the pre-merge state completely: index, working tree, and the removal of MERGE_HEAD. Until you commit, a merge is always fully reversible — this is the escape hatch worth knowing before you need it.
steps.expect: Clean tree, main's version of config.yaml, tuning.md gone again.

verify.label: the abort left a clean tree

steps.title: Turn on a conflict style that shows the base
steps.why: The default markers show only the two sides. `diff3` (or `zdiff3`) adds the common ancestor between them, so you can see what each side actually changed rather than guessing.

steps.title: Resolve using the base as evidence
steps.why: Now the reasoning is visible: the base was 3, we went to 5 after an incident, they went to 10 for a flaky upstream. 10 is the safer answer and the base told you why.

steps.title: Now the automatic tie-breakers
steps.why: `-X ours` resolves conflicting hunks in favour of the branch you are on, still merging everything non-conflicting. It is a time-saver for generated files and lockfiles — and a silent bug factory for source code.
commands: git merge -X ours -m "Merge side-branch, preferring our config" side-branch
steps.expect: Our retries survive; region changed to us-east-1 because that hunk did not conflict.

verify.label: -X ours still merged the non-conflicting change
verify.hint: that is the difference between -X ours and -s ours

steps.title: The dangerous sibling
steps.why: `-s ours` ignores the other tree completely. The merge commit records side-branch as a parent, so git will consider it merged forever, but not one line of it was taken.
commands: git merge -s ours -m "Record side-branch as merged without taking it" side-branch
steps.expect: config.yaml is untouched — still main's merged version — despite a merge commit with two parents.

verify.label: -s ours discarded the other side entirely, region change included
verify.hint: compare with the -X ours result, which did take the region change

steps.title: Go back to the real result
steps.why: The experiment branches were for demonstration. main holds the merge you resolved by hand, which is the one you would actually ship.

verify.label: main's merge kept the right value from each side
verify.hint: resolve by reading the base, not by picking a side

verify.label: the three-way conflict style is enabled
main's tip is the merge commit

pitfalls: `-X ours` and `-s ours` differ by one letter and by everything else. Read the command twice before running it on a shared branch.
`-X ours` on source code silently drops a colleague's fix inside a conflicting hunk. Reserve it for generated files, lockfiles and changelogs.
`git merge --abort` only works before the merge commit exists. Afterwards you need `git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD`.
`zdiff3` is strictly more informative than the default `merge` style. Turn it on globally and never look back.
cheatsheet: undo a merge you already committed
show the common ancestor in conflicts
prefer our side in conflicting hunks only
prefer their side in conflicting hunks
record as merged, take nothing — rarely correct
stage the merge but let you inspect before committing
